**1. Does `deleteComment` check who wrote the comment? No.**
- `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` requires a login, because `AuthMiddleware` is applied to it in `article.module.ts:29`. It does not check who wrote the comment.
- The controller (`article.controller.ts:85`) never reads the current user. It passes only `slug` and `id` to the service.
- The service (`article.service.ts:114`) takes no user id. It looks the comment up and deletes it.
- Nothing could be compared even if it tried. `Comment` (`comment.entity.ts`) has only `id`, `body` and `article`, with no author column. `addComment` doesn't record an author either.
- So any logged-in user can delete any comment.
- Separately, `deleteComment` throws a `TypeError` (a 500) when the comment `id` doesn't exist, because `comment.id` is read from `undefined` (`article.service.ts:118`).

**2. Profile routes and the auth middleware**

| Route | Middleware | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /profiles/:username` | No | Optional auth. The `@User` decorator reads the JWT from the header itself if the middleware hasn't set `req.user` (`user.decorator.ts:12-17`). |
| `POST /profiles/:username/follow` | Yes | Registered in `profile.module.ts:22` |
| `DELETE /profiles/:username/follow` | Yes | Same registration, which uses `RequestMethod.ALL` |

**3. What the `RO` suffix means**
- It stands for **Response Object**. This is stated in `.claude/knowledge/workspace.md:62`.
- Each `<Thing>RO` interface is the JSON envelope a handler returns, for example `ArticleRO` is `{ article }` and `ProfileRO` is `{ profile }`.
- `LESSONS.md` (#57) says a handler returning a bare entity instead of a `*RO` is a bug.

I only read the code. I haven't changed anything. Adding an author to comments and checking it in `deleteComment` would mean a new column and a changed service signature. Tell me if you want that.
